title: Maximization of nuclear fusion reactivity via optimal energy distributions
authors: Roberto Onofrio, Kamel Ourabah, Carlo Presilla
abstract: We investigate the optimization of nuclear fusion reactivity relative to the choice of energy probability distribution. A single Maxwell-Boltzmann (MB) distribution is found to be optimal in the region where reactivity is a concave function of the average available kinetic energy, specifically near the reactivity peak. Conversely, in regions where the reactivity curve is convex, optimization is achieved through a bimodal MB distribution. We then discuss our results in the context of three classes of generalized energy distributions (superstatistics), which are modeled as a continuum of MB distributions. As expected, in all cases examined, the reactivity gains provided by superstatistics are bounded by the proposed optimal distribution. Finally, we apply these findings to deuterium-deuterium and deuterium-tritium fusion processes using empirical parametrizations of their respective cross sections. For both reactions, employing optimal bimodal MB distributions at low average energies-of particular interest for magnetically confined plasmas-yields a reactivity enhancement of approximately a factor of 2.
summary: This work theoretically maximizes nuclear fusion reactivity by optimizing the energy distribution of colliding ions beyond the standard Maxwell-Boltzmann assumption. It proves that the optimal distribution switches between single and bimodal forms depending on the energy regime's concavity. The findings suggest that engineered bimodal distributions can significantly boost fusion reactivity for practical plasma applications.
main_problem: The paper investigates how optimizing the energy probability distribution of colliding ions can maximize the nuclear fusion reactivity compared to using the standard Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution.
main_result: The optimal distribution is found to be a single Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution when reactivity is concave, but a bimodal MB distribution when the reactivity curve is convex, yielding up to a factor of 2 enhancement for DD/DT fusion at low energies.
method: The optimization is treated as a constrained variational problem, using mathematical tools like Jensen's inequality to determine the optimal probability density function (PDF) that maximizes the average reactivity.
model_or_system: The system is nuclear fusion (DD and DT reactions), modeled by averaging the cross-section $\sigma(E)$ and velocity $v(E)$ over a general energy probability distribution $P(E)$. The framework extends to superstatistics, which models the distribution as a continuum of MB distributions.
key_observables: Reactivity $\langle\sigma vangle$, energy probability distribution $P(E)$, and the reactivity enhancement factor.
important_parameters: Average available kinetic energy ($\mu_0$), inverse temperature ($ eta$), and the specific fusion cross-sections for DD and DT reactions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the reactivity function $\langle\sigma vangle$ can be analyzed for concavity/convexity regimes, and it models the system using continuous mixtures of MB distributions (superstatistics).
figures_summary: Figures are referenced to show the probability distributions for different superstatistics types and expected reactivity gains for DD and DT reactions.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the general optimization framework using variational calculus, derives the optimal distribution structure based on the concavity of the reactivity function, and finally applies these theoretical findings to specific physical systems like DD and DT fusion.
why_interesting: While focused on fusion, the core mathematical technique—optimizing expectation values over non-standard energy distributions (superstatistics) when the underlying function is non-concave—is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics in complex quantum systems.
